system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A cap of at least **50% of price (AUD 12m)** for general warranties, with separate higher or uncapped treatment for fundamental, tax, indemnity, covenant and fraud claims. | **Reject 20% and counter at 50%** — AUD 4.8m gives inadequate recourse for material warranty failures in a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** deductible basket, so only excess is recoverable. | Lower de minimis, e.g. **AUD 10,000**, and a lower **tipping basket**, e.g. AUD 150,000, after which all qualifying loss is recoverable; related claims aggregated. | **Counter with AUD 10k / AUD 150k tipping thresholds** — the proposed deductible structure leaves a material first-loss layer with Buyer and may fragment related claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**; Seller seeks limitations to apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with notification preserving a claim until finally resolved and separate periods for other categories. | **Extend to 24 months and confine it to general warranties** — 18 months may not cover two audit/reporting cycles and must not truncate tax, title or indemnity claims. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same **20% cap, thresholds and 18-month limit** as general warranties. | Fundamental, capacity and title claims capped at **100% of price**, with no de minimis/basket and a substantially longer period, preferably no contractual expiry for title. | **Reject general-regime treatment** — Buyer must have full-price recourse if Seller lacked capacity or did not transfer the shares and title promised. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Exclusive-remedy, non-reliance and limitation provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**; no express fraud carve-out is offered. | Express disapplication of all caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge and exclusive-remedy provisions for **fraud, dishonesty, fraudulent concealment and wilful misconduct**. | **Insert a comprehensive fraud carve-out** — Seller must not benefit from contractual protections where information was deliberately falsified or concealed. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature, scope and likely consequences, against identified warranties; agreed data-room snapshot/index attached. | **Delete general disclosure and require specific fair disclosure** — dumping documents or relying on public records should not transfer the disclosure risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything **discoverable** from the data room or public records. | At most, actual conscious knowledge of a short list of named senior Buyer personnel, without adviser knowledge, constructive knowledge or duty of inquiry; Seller bears the proof burden. | **Delete constructive and adviser knowledge** — warranties allocate risk to Seller and should not be defeated by what Buyer could theoretically have discovered. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of the counterparty’s written consent, although conditions under clause 11.3 remain unproven. | A Completion condition requiring **final, unconditional and effective consent**, satisfaction or waiver of all associated conditions, and no adverse amendment, fee or termination right without Buyer approval. | **Make full Bluefen consent a hard CP, waivable only by Buyer** — the contract represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and bare delivery of conditional consent is insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; release is to be provided **after Completion**. | Repayment from Seller’s Completion proceeds and delivery **at or before Completion** of executed releases, discharges, payout confirmation and control of registrations, consistent with debt-free/cash-free terms. | **Do not complete against a post-Completion promise** — Buyer must acquire the Company debt-free and free of Riverlark security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD **420,000** Completion bonuses are said to be Seller’s matter and are omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unclear. | Treat all bonuses and on-costs triggered by the sale as **Seller transaction costs/debt-like items**, fully quantified and paid or deducted from Completion proceeds, with an indemnity for any residual liability. | **Add the full grossed-up amount to funds flow as a Seller deduction** — the liability is Completion-triggered and must not reduce the debt-free/cash-free value delivered to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific **AUD 180,000 SOW3 payment**. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Payment before Completion, written confirmation that all SOW3 fees are cleared and Project Materials/IP vest in the Company, plus a specific indemnity covering payment, ownership defects, infringement, remediation and related loss. | **Expand the indemnity and require chain-of-title evidence** — paying AUD 180,000 alone does not establish that critical IP has transferred or protect against ownership loss. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification obligations remain unresolved. | Prompt forensic investigation, containment and documented legal assessment before Completion; compliance with notification/remediation duties; ongoing cooperation and a specific indemnity or escrow for all pre-Completion consequences. | **Require resolution and ring-fenced recourse** — the possible exposure of about 1,240 records creates uncertain regulatory, customer and remediation risk. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Evidence of timing, termination rights, service periods and accrual treatment; no entry into or renewal of material contracts before Completion without Buyer consent; appropriate working-capital/debt-like adjustment. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without evidence** — Buyer must not inherit unpriced or avoidable commitments entered into for Seller’s benefit. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks to apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions across **all Claims**, unless expressly stated otherwise. | Express claim categories with tailored regimes: general warranties; fundamental/title; tax; specific indemnities; covenants; purchase-price/debt adjustments; equitable relief; and fraud. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture by claim category** — a single general regime could inadvertently cap or time-bar negotiated dollar-for-dollar protections and Completion obligations. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies solely on the Company share register at DD-012 as evidence that it owns 100% of the shares. | ASIC searches, constitution and historical registers, share certificates, issue/transfer documents, beneficial ownership confirmation, evidence of no options or third-party rights, and Completion delivery of executed transfers and certificates. | **Require complete legal and beneficial title evidence** — a company-maintained register alone does not exclude competing interests, defects or undisclosed securities. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP warranties as settled under the general **20% / 18-month** regime. | A separate tax deed/indemnity with 100% cap and claims period extending beyond applicable statutory review periods; robust IP ownership, validity, licensing, open-source, infringement and employee/contractor assignment warranties with enhanced survival and recourse. | **Keep tax and IP terms open and separately negotiate them** — latent tax liabilities and defective IP ownership can emerge well after 18 months and materially impair enterprise value. |

**Overall:** The package is materially Seller-favourable. The priority Completion blockers are Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment and releases, Ironquay chain of title, proper treatment of the bonuses, and investigation of the export/privacy incident.
=== END ADVICE ===
